title: A W Tozer Said “What comes into our minds when we think about God is the most important thing about us.”
scripture_text: Reading and understanding the beatitudes can be a daunting experience, they are anti cultural, they challenge how most people think, they redefine priorities and they revolutionise lives. They are like verbalised missiles that destroy tightly held belief systems. They redefine our understanding of our humanity, and show us how to really experience God.
devotional:
Many of us are content to live with a dysfunctional view of God, we often try to reconstruct God into something we want him to be, we can use our circumstances to interpret God for us, and often we end up with a wrong and unbiblical view of Him.

Often our ‘seeing’ of God can be distorted and intermittent. Sometimes we are very sure of what God is doing in our lives, but more often than not, we are less sure, we can feel confused and unsure how to make sense of our situations. Maybe you have earnestly brought a circumstance or a situation to God, hoping God would intervene, and he hasn’t. Maybe you have had a genuine need that God doesn’t seem to meet, and you don’t understand why? And you can’t see God, or if you do see him, you do not like what you see.

It is so easy for any one of us to live with a dysfunctional view of God. And not see God for whom he really is, and see him for whom we think he is.

To have a proper view of God, requires deep, radical transformation within us so we have a capacity to comprehend God in some measure. When Jesus speaks about seeing God, he is not talking about our theological understanding, but how we most frequently relate to God.

Often we do not really express how we perceive God; often our relationship with God is tied up with some hidden agenda or alternative motive, causing us to have a blurred- lined theology, [i.e. a confused and unhealthy understanding of God.] How we really perceive God is ingrained within us, and often there is a distorted view of God ingrained deep within our hearts

For example, sometimes we relate to God the same way people relate to the ‘banker’ in television programme ‘Deal or No Deal!’ We have at set of conditions in our mind that has become the basis of our Relationship with God. We think if I do all the right things, then God will come through for me, I deserve God’s blessings, I have earned enough brownie points for God to answer my prayers. We would never verbalise this kind of thinking, but deep within us, perhaps this is how we often view God. Our seeing of God is distorted.

Not seeing God can be a scary distressing experience, it can make a person feel vulnerable, confused and very alone. There are dark periods in our lives when it seems impossible to discern or detect God, we are groping for some kind of understanding, grasping for some kind of sense of what we are experiencing. It is at times like this, this beatitude come to our aid. ‘Blessed are the pure in heart for they shall see God.’

If we are going to recognise God as God then we need to experience a pure heart. So what I want to do, over the next few days, is help us grasp what Jesus means when he speaks about a pure heart, and look at the external evidences of a pure heart.
prayer: Father thank you that our relationship with you is based on Your grace that has been poured out for me.

A W Tozer Said “What comes into our minds when we think about God is the most important thing about us.”

Study Text: Pure in heart part 1
Reading and understanding the beatitudes can be a daunting experience, they are anti cultural, they challenge how most people think, they redefine priorities and they revolutionise lives. They are like verbalised missiles that destroy tightly held belief systems. They redefine our understanding of our humanity, and show us how to really experience God.

Many of us are content to live with a dysfunctional view of God, we often try to reconstruct God into something we want him to be, we can use our circumstances to interpret God for us, and often we end up with a wrong and unbiblical view of Him.

Prayer: Father thank you that our relationship with you is based on Your grace that has been poured out for me.
